headline: Revenue jumps on M&A, but profits fall and guidance is cut
summary_short: Group revenue rose 17.4% y/y to $4,304M on the Snai and Betnacional acquisitions and a favorable y/y swing in sports results. Net income fell 34.9% y/y to $216M and diluted EPS dropped 21.7% to $1.23 as Flutter cut full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.305bn and $2.865bn at the midpoint.
summary_long: Revenue grew 17.4% y/y to $4,304M on the Snai and Betnacional acquisitions and a favorable sports-results swing. US revenue rose 6% (sportsbook +1%, iGaming +19%) as the sportsbook improvement plan gained traction; International revenue rose 27% while organic revenue was flat on unfavorable sports results. Net income fell 34.9% y/y to $216M and diluted EPS fell 21.7% to $1.23 on higher interest expense and D&A from M&A, partly offset by a larger non-cash Fox Option benefit. Flutter cut FY2026 guidance to $18.305bn revenue / $2.865bn adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint (from $18.4bn/$2.97bn) on Q1 sports-results headwinds and Arkansas launch costs. Cash fell to $1,512M; long-term debt rose to $11,965M; leverage held at 3.7x.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects the Snai and Betnacional acquisitions plus a favorable y/y swing in sports results; AMPs fell 3% on the India market closure.
Release attributes (adjusted) EBITDA growth to revenue growth, offset by FanDuel Predicts investment and new-state launch costs.
Fell on higher interest expense and D&A from M&A, partly offset by a larger non-cash Fox Option benefit.
Declined with net income, partly offset by a y/y benefit from non-controlling interests.
Quarter-over-quarter decline reflects repayment of the revolving credit facility; the y/y increase is not explained in the release.
CEO called Q1 'encouraging' on US sportsbook improvement and local-hero M&A in Italy and Brazil, while announcing management changes to sharpen US focus.
